questions.question: Regulatory signs are usually ____ and must always be obeyed.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs control how traffic moves. They are white with black markings. All drivers must obey them.

questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes show arrows to control turns from specific lanes. A green arrow means:

options.text: It is used only on one-way streets.
You can go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
You can only proceed if a green circular light appears with the arrow.
It points to the nearest airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means the same as a green light. However, traffic in that lane must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: What should you do if your accelerator sticks while driving?

options.text: Reach down and pull it up.
Shift to neutral and press the brake steadily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake steadily.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Shift into neutral and press the brake steadily. When safe, pull off the road and turn off the engine.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Emotions affect your driving ability. If you are worried, excited, afraid, angry, or sad, you may not drive well. Stress makes it hard to concentrate on driving. It is better to wait to drive than to drive while upset.

questions.question: When approaching an uncontrolled intersection, a driver should:

options.text: Keep the same speed and go through.
Stop, look all around, and then go.
Let all other drivers go first.

questions.explanation: At an intersection with no stop sign or traffic signal, yield to vehicles coming from the right. Always be ready to yield to avoid a crash. Ease off the accelerator, cover the brake, and look left, right, and left again.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Drive the same way as on dry roads.

questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between you and the car ahead. Your car will take longer to stop on slippery surfaces than on dry roads.

questions.question: What happens if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
The alcohol helps the medicine cure a cold.
The combination can increase the effects of the alcohol or medicine.
There is no effect because they are different.

questions.correctAnswerText: The combination can increase the effects of the alcohol or medicine.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with medicine can increase how much each affects your body. For example, one drink with a cold remedy could affect you as much as several drinks without medication.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing with a standard crossbuck sign but no gates or flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Approach carefully and cross only when you know no train is coming.
Turn down your radio to listen for an approaching train.
Only continue when a flagger tells you it is safe to cross.

questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings carefully and cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. If a flagger is present, follow their instructions.

questions.question: When approaching an accident scene, you should:

options.text: Stop only if you are involved or if emergency help has not arrived yet.

questions.explanation: Do not stop unless you are involved or emergency help has not arrived. Keep your attention on driving and watch for people on or near the road. Do not stop just to look at an accident.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: No more dangerous than normal driving.

questions.explanation: Distracted driving is very dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers at risk. Paying attention to driving helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: You should drive with extra caution near a pedestrian using a white cane because:

options.text: The person is a police officer.

questions.explanation: A white cane means the pedestrian is blind. Slow down and yield the right-of-way. Be ready to stop to protect the pedestrian.

questions.question: A red circle with a slash through it on a sign means:

options.text: Some drivers should yield to others.

questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash is a prohibition sign. It tells you that an action is not allowed.

questions.question: You must stop for a school bus:

options.text: That is parked on the shoulder with no children in it.
When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.
On a two-lane highway when its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a two-lane highway when its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: Stop when you see a school bus with red lights flashing on a two-lane road. Traffic from both directions must stop. Stay stopped while the red lights flash and the stop arm is out.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Drive at the speed limit with caution.

questions.explanation: Slow down when you see rain, snow, or ice. These conditions make roads slippery. You may need to drive slower than the speed limit for safety.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes mean?

options.text: You may pass, even if it is dangerous.
You may pass if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate lanes going the same direction. You can cross them to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Car drivers should know that large trucks:

options.text: Do not need more space than cars.

questions.explanation: Large trucks have big blind spots in front, on the sides, and in back. Avoid these areas. Trucks need more space to turn and stop than cars do.

questions.question: If you notice a vehicle defect that could affect safety, you should:

options.text: Fix it as soon as possible.
Fix it when you have money.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix it as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Any defect that affects safe operation must be fixed right away. Fix problems before driving the vehicle.

questions.question: A driver entering interstate traffic from an entrance or acceleration ramp:

options.text: Should yield to drivers already on the interstate.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume that other drivers will move for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the interstate.
questions.explanation: When entering an interstate from a ramp, you must yield to traffic already on the highway. Merge into traffic safely when you have a clear space.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road curves right ahead. Slow to the safe speed shown.
A divided highway starts. Slow to the safe speed shown.
Merge ahead. Slow to the safe speed shown.
The road winds ahead. Slow to the safe speed shown.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right ahead. Slow to the safe speed shown.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the road curves to the right. Slow down to the speed listed on the sign (35 mph in this case).

questions.question: Orange signs are:
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn of work zones. They are usually diamond-shaped with black letters. They tell you that workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight ahead.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill next to a curb, turn your steering wheel away from the curb. If your car rolls, it will roll into the curb and stop.

questions.question: The main reason drinking alcohol and driving is so dangerous is that it affects your:
questions.explanation: Alcohol reaches your brain 20 to 40 minutes after you drink it. It affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and skill.

questions.question: What may help drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Sitting in their driveways with their cars running.

questions.explanation: Every quick stop uses time and fuel to speed back up. Drivers who look ahead can slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid hard braking. This saves gas.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a flagger is ahead controlling traffic in a construction area.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The left lane is reserved for vehicles with a specific number of occupants.
Specific turning movements are allowed from specific lanes.
Drivers in both lanes are responsible for merging smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane is reserved for vehicles with a specific number of occupants.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lane. HOV lanes are for buses and vehicles with a driver plus one or more passengers.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while you drive. You should:

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the ignition.
Turn on your hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer with extra effort, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer with extra effort, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: If your power steering stops, you will need to use more force to steer. Reduce your speed and pull off the road to stop in a safe place.

questions.question: Distracted drivers are more likely to crash when using which of the following?
questions.explanation: Cell phones, radios, and CD players can all distract you while driving and increase your risk of a crash.

questions.question: Many crashes are caused by:

options.text: Drivers traveling too fast for the conditions.
Drivers consistently checking their mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers maintaining a four-second following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers traveling too fast for the conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers go too fast for the conditions. Always drive within speed limits and slow down when conditions are poor.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, you should:
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians. If you think another driver is about to hit you, sound your horn.

questions.question: The space you need to cross traffic depends on:

options.text: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
The presence of a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
